items.title: Russian drones reportedly strike Izmail port facilities and cargo vessel
items.summary: Russian forces reportedly carried out overnight drone strikes on port infrastructure at Izmail used to unload and store military supplies. The same account alleges a dry-cargo vessel carrying dual-use goods toward the port of Pivdennyi was also hit at sea; details of the damage were not provided.

items.title: Russia claims capture of Zalivne amid fighting in Zaporizhzhia
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry reportedly announced the capture of Zalivne on the Tersyanka–Voskresenka sector of the Zaporizhzhia front. Fighting was also reported near Orikhiv and Novodanylivka, with Russian forces said to be expanding their positions west of Orikhiv.

items.title: Russian drone strikes reportedly target four locomotives in Dnipro and Zaporizhzhia
items.summary: Footage circulated of reported Geran drone strikes on railway locomotives, including three in Dnipro and one in Zaporizhzhia. The account identifies four separate targets but does not establish the extent of damage or whether rail operations were disrupted.

items.title: Russia says air defences intercepted 184 Ukrainian drones overnight
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry said its air defences destroyed 184 Ukrainian fixed-wing drones between the evening of November 17 and the morning of November 18 over Belgorod and Rostov regions, Krasnodar Krai, Crimea and the Sea of Azov. The ministry did not provide a detailed breakdown of damage or casualties in the cited update.

items.title: Gas carrier reportedly struck by drones off Bulgaria
items.summary: The Liberian-flagged gas carrier GAS HUSKY, reportedly carrying 3,400 tonnes of propane and described as linked to Ukraine's gas fleet, was allegedly hit by four drones roughly 100 kilometres off Bulgaria's coast. Footage circulating online appears to show the vessel burning; the extent of damage and any casualties were not specified.

items.title: Ukrainian lawmaker says recruitment-centre confrontations have declined
items.summary: Ukrainian parliamentary defence committee member Fedir Venislavskyi said confrontations involving territorial recruitment centres have largely subsided. He added that men aged 50–60 are being mobilized less often, although they remain eligible for conscription.

items.title: Drone attacks reportedly injure eight in Krasnodar Krai and Adygea
items.summary: Regional authorities reportedly said overnight Ukrainian drone attacks injured eight people across Krasnodar Krai and Adygea. Drone debris sparked fires at two enterprises in Krasnodar Krai, while an apartment building in Enem, Adygea, was struck, with four people reportedly injured there.

items.title: Russia reportedly proposes NATO troop limits in wider Ukraine negotiations
items.summary: A reported Russian proposal would bar NATO troop deployments in countries that joined the alliance after 1997 in exchange for reducing Russia's military presence in Kaliningrad and Belarus. The account says US representatives have discussed European troop deployments and security arrangements with Russia and Ukraine as part of possible war-ending terms; European leaders reportedly opposed withdrawing NATO forces from Eastern Europe.

items.title: Power outages reported in parts of Kyiv after strikes
items.summary: Several districts of Kyiv reportedly lost electricity following strikes on the Ukrainian capital. The affected districts, number of customers and expected restoration times were not specified in the initial account.

items.title: Ukrainian lawmaker alleges major misuse of Kyiv energy-protection funds
items.summary: Ukrainian parliament member Nagorniak reportedly alleged that up to 700 million hryvnias of an 800-million-hryvnia allocation for protecting energy infrastructure in Kyiv region went to contractors unrelated to building the defenses. The figures and alleged misuse are attributed to his account, rather than established findings of an investigation.

items.title: Finland's president rejects report of Russian demand to leave NATO
items.summary: Finnish President Alexander Stubb denied a Bild account alleging that Russia had demanded Finland withdraw from NATO during talks in Abu Dhabi. He urged readers not to take the reported proposal seriously, according to comments cited by Finnish newspaper Ilta-Sanomat.

items.title: Crew of stricken gas carrier reportedly rescued off Bulgaria
items.summary: All 19 crew members of the Liberian-flagged GAS HUSKY were reportedly rescued by Bulgarian forces after the vessel caught fire and sank off Bulgaria's coast. Two sailors reportedly sustained minor injuries; the account says the ship had been sailing from Alexandria toward Romania's Midia port when it was struck by an unidentified weapon.

items.title: Russia says it hit Ukrainian drone facilities and downed 310 drones
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry said its forces struck Ukrainian drone manufacturing and storage sites over the past day and that air defenses shot down 310 fixed-wing Ukrainian drones. The ministry also estimated Ukrainian personnel losses at around 1,165, a battlefield figure that remains a Russian military assertion.

items.title: US and European representatives set for Berlin talks on Ukraine security
items.summary: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are reportedly due to meet Ukrainian and European representatives in Berlin on November 19 to discuss security guarantees and Ukraine's post-war economic recovery. The planned meeting comes amid differences over ceasefire terms and Europe's role in negotiations.

items.title: Kremlin says Putin and Xi discussed Ukraine settlement in Shenzhen
items.summary: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping discussed efforts to settle the war in Ukraine during their talks in Shenzhen. Putin also mentioned his contacts with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner in Moscow; no new agreement was announced.

items.title: Russian ambassador disputes Moldova's protest over drone incursions
items.summary: Russia's ambassador called Moldova's diplomatic protest over recent drone incursions unfounded, suggested Ukraine might be behind the incidents and proposed a joint investigation. His remarks follow Moldovan accounts of drones entering its airspace; responsibility for the incidents remains disputed.

items.title: EU Commission proposes €45 billion for Ukraine in 2027
items.summary: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen has proposed €45 billion in funding for Ukraine in 2027, saying it would cover roughly two-thirds of the country's projected needs. She expects partners to provide another €25 billion, with EU leaders scheduled to discuss the proposal at an emergency summit on November 26–27.

items.title: US House Republicans reportedly seek Ukraine aid cuts in defence bill
items.summary: Republican lawmakers are reportedly pushing to remove provisions on military assistance and intelligence sharing with Ukraine from the annual US defence authorization bill, alongside proposed sanctions on Russia. The changes are described as part of negotiations over congressional oversight, with the bill's final text expected in early December.

items.title: Sweden announces additional Ukraine military funding and Gripen support arrangements
items.summary: Sweden reportedly announced about $71 million in additional contributions to military-support funds for Ukraine, including air defence, long-range capabilities and US weapons procurement. A separate Swedish-British-Ukrainian arrangement concerns ammunition, equipment and spare parts for Gripen fighter aircraft.

items.title: EU reportedly hesitant to include Russian oil shipping ban in next sanctions package
items.summary: The European Commission may leave a proposed ban on maritime transport of Russian oil out of its 22nd sanctions package over concerns that member states would block it, according to a report attributed to Bloomberg. A similar proposal was reportedly removed during negotiations over the previous package.

items.title: German foreign minister rejects proposal for new European security architecture
items.summary: German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul rejected a Russian proposal for a new European security framework, arguing that existing agreed rules and principles should instead be respected. His response underscores continuing differences over the security arrangements surrounding negotiations on Ukraine.

items.title: Kyiv issues detailed bridge restrictions following November 17 strikes
items.summary: Kyiv authorities reportedly limited the South Bridge to lighter vehicles and public transport, while restricting the North Bridge to public transport and emergency vehicles. The Podilskyi Bridge faces temporary closures during air alerts, and the Paton Bridge is operating one-way on a timed schedule; two other crossings remain unrestricted.

items.title: Russian aircraft manufacturer delivers another batch of Su-34 bombers
items.summary: Russia's United Aircraft Corporation announced another delivery of Su-34 fighter-bombers to the Defence Ministry after factory testing, describing it as the third publicly announced batch this year. The number of aircraft was not disclosed; the Su-34 is widely used to deploy glide bombs in the war.

items.title: Patriot missile production reportedly constrained by specialist French material
items.summary: The Pentagon reportedly faces a shortage of carbonised rayon used in the rocket motors of Patriot PAC-3 MSE interceptors, with the sole approved supplier, France's ArianeGroup, unable to rapidly expand deliveries. The reported bottleneck comes as Ukraine seeks more Patriot missiles from allied stockpiles; a new US production facility is not expected until 2030.

items.title: Geran drone reportedly strikes hangar housing An-124 at Hostomel airfield
items.summary: Footage reportedly shows a Russian Geran drone striking a hangar at Hostomel airfield near Kyiv where an An-124 Ruslan heavy transport aircraft was parked. The aircraft had reportedly remained in Ukraine since 2022 after maintenance left it unable to depart; the extent of any damage is unclear.

items.title: New images reportedly show damage at Motor Sich plant in Zaporizhzhia
items.summary: Images circulated showing the reported aftermath of strikes on a building within the Motor Sich factory grounds in Zaporizhzhia on November 17. The account identified a location at the industrial complex but did not specify the building's function or the extent of damage.

items.title: Russian military says FPV drones destroyed two Ukrainian UAV control posts
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry said FPV drone operators from its Southern Group of Forces destroyed two Ukrainian drone-control positions. The brief announcement did not identify the exact locations or provide further operational details.
